markets.text: The Ale Index closes at {drinks} today. Analysts describe the mood on the stockpile floor as 'thirsty but professional.'
Prepared meals stand at {meals}, raw meat at {meat}, plants at {plants}. Past performance does not guarantee dinner.
Gems are trading at {gems} units. The jewellers' guild calls that 'plenty of sparkle' and declined to elaborate.
Metal bars held steady at {bars} this session, as the forge district awaits further word from the smelters.
Timber reserves sit at {wood} logs. Sources close to the carpenters say every single one is already spoken for.
Stone is at {stone} units, which experts confirm is 'a lot of rocks.' We'll keep you posted.
The Cat Census reports {cats} cats in the fort. The cats have declined to confirm or deny this figure.
Quick look at the board: drink {drinks}, meals {meals}, gems {gems}, bars {bars}. The board is a slab. We are proud of the slab.
In stone futures, {stone} units remain on hand. Masons call the market 'solid.' Masons call everything solid.
Wood at {wood}, stone at {stone}. Traders say the eternal rivalry between the two remains, as ever, entirely one-sided.
The mood on the trading floor is calm today, mostly because the trading floor is a stockpile and nobody is on it.
{citizen}, a local hauler, tells DNN the {meals} meals in storage 'look fine' and 'smell mostly fine.' A strong market signal.
Bars at {bars}. The metalsmiths' index rose on rumours of a new anvil, which turned out to be the old anvil, moved.
Gems at {gems}. The broker who claimed a rough gem 'is basically cut already' has been asked to leave the stockpile.
Plants in storage: {plants}. The farmers' cooperative calls it a 'leafy quarter' and asks that you stop mentioning cave spiders.
Year to date, the Ale Index has outperformed every other index in {fort}, largely because it is the only index anyone checks.
The bookkeeper confirms today's numbers are accurate 'to within a few barrels, or possibly a few hundred.' Back to you.
Stock summary for {month}: drinks {drinks}, meat {meat}, plants {plants}. The market remains open, because it has no door.
Analysts note {cats} cats and {meat} units of meat in the fort, and ask that the two figures be kept in separate rooms.
{anchor2} reports the bar market at {bars}: copper, iron, and 'a bit of something shiny the smelter won't name.'
Cut and rough gems total {gems}. The jewellers urge calm, patience, and very dark lighting in the gem stockpile.
Breaking on the Ale Index: drinks have fallen to {drinks}. The brewers are being asked to brew, and to brew now.
The Ale Index is down to {drinks}. Traders were seen wiping their beards in what experts call 'pre-tantrum posture.'
With only {drinks} drinks in reserve, the tavern keeper has begun pouring smaller mugs and calling them 'artisanal.'
Drinks at {drinks}. DNN advises viewers to stay calm, stay hydrated, and absolutely not drink the water.
Ale reserves sit at a worrying {drinks}. {citizen} was overheard asking whether the well 'counts.' It does not count.
Panic selling on the drink floor as stocks dip to {drinks}. There is nothing left to sell. That is the panic.
{anchor} here with grim numbers: just {drinks} drinks left. The farmers say help is coming. Slowly. Through fermentation.
Drinks are down to {drinks}, and the still is reportedly 'very busy' and asks that you 'please stop knocking.'
Drink supply has slipped to {drinks}. Economists call it a sobriety event. Dwarves are calling it much worse things.
The Ale Index is surging at {drinks}! Analysts say the market is bullish, and also slightly tipsy.
Drinks hit {drinks} today. The tavern reports a sharp rise in singing and a sharp fall in productivity.
With {drinks} drinks in stock, the brewers have declared a holiday. The holiday is called 'today.'
At {drinks} drinks, the ale market is so strong the coopers are now the busiest dwarves in {fort}.
Drinks at {drinks}. Economists warn of a bubble. The bubbles are in the ale. They're fine.
{drinks} drinks on hand. {anchor2} calls it 'a golden age.' The ale is also golden. Coincidence? Our panel says no.
The drink stockpile is overflowing at {drinks}. Haulers report carrying barrels into rooms that were never built for barrels.
Ale Index up big at {drinks}. Sources close to the stockpile say morale is high and the stockpile is, frankly, glowing.
Food stocks are thin: {meals} prepared meals and {plants} plants. The cook says he is 'getting creative.' That is not reassuring.
Meals are down to {meals}. The dining hall has been rebranded 'the waiting hall' until further notice.
With just {meals} meals in storage, the kitchen is now accepting suggestions, donations and well-behaved mushrooms.
Food is scarce at {meals} meals. {citizen} reports seeing a hungry dwarf look at a cat for a very long time.
Meals: {meals}. Plants: {plants}. Farmers are planting faster, which, they remind us, is not how farming works.
Food supply has fallen to {meals}. Analysts recommend diversifying into roasts, biscuits, and basically anything edible.
DNN is told the fort has {meals} meals left. The cook asks that viewers 'please stop staring at the kitchen.'
Meals at {meals}. The fishery has been asked to fish harder. The fishery has asked what that means.
Low food this {season}: {meals} meals. The nobles' dinner has been downgraded from 'feast' to 'a plate.'
Food is booming: {meals} prepared meals in the larder. The cooks are taking a well-earned bow, and a biscuit.
With {meals} meals on hand, the dining hall reports record attendance and a record number of second helpings.
Meals at {meals}, plants at {plants}. Analysts describe the food sector as 'stuffed,' which is also how they feel.
The food market is strong at {meals} meals. The kitchen has started labelling its roasts by vintage.
{meals} meals in storage. The cook says the larder is 'full to the rafters.' The fort has no rafters, so this is a big claim.
Food stocks top {meals}. Economists say no dwarf in {fort} goes hungry this {season}, barring a carp incident.
Plants climb to {plants}. The farmers are celebrating by not farming for one entire afternoon.
A strong day for food at {meals} meals. Stockpile insiders predict the haulers will complain about it by nightfall.
Meat is down to {meat} units. The butcher is pacing the shop and the livestock are pretending not to notice.
Meat stocks at a lean {meat}. Hunters have been sent out with crossbows, optimism, and a packed lunch of mostly bread.
Only {meat} meat left. The butcher says demand is 'robust' and supply is 'a philosophical question.'
Meat at {meat}. The fishery offers carp as an alternative. Viewers are reminded the carp would say the same about you.
With {meat} meat in storage, the kitchen now serves roasts that are 'mostly plant, with meat in spirit.'
The meat index is weak at {meat}. Sources in the pasture say the yaks have called a meeting.
Meat sitting at {meat}. The hunters blame the weather, the elves, and in one case, a particularly fast rabbit.
Meat reserves: {meat}. The butcher has started sharpening knives loudly, which analysts read as a buy signal.
The Cat Census now stands at {cats}. Analysts call the cat sector 'overvalued, but impossible to short.'
{cats} cats in {fort} today. Every one of them has adopted a dwarf. None of the dwarves were consulted.
With {cats} cats, the fort's vermin market has completely collapsed. The rats have applied for relief.
Cats at {cats}. The animal handler confirms that is 'too many cats' and that he 'loves every single one.'
The cat population hits {cats}. Haulers report the stockpiles are now about forty percent cat by volume.
{cats} cats and rising. Economists warned of a cat bubble, then noticed a cat sitting on their charts.
Cat futures soar to {cats}. The tavern has begun charging cats a cover fee. No cat has paid.
Experts estimate {cats} cats, but admit some may have been counted twice because they moved.

ads.text: DNN is brought to you by Deepbarrel Ale. Deepbarrel: because water is for washing, and washing is optional.
This hour of DNN is sponsored by the Fort Hospital. Broken leg? Broken arm? Broken everything? We have a bed. Probably.
DNN is brought to you by Coffinworks Masonry. Quality slabs, roomy caskets, engraving at no extra charge. Plan ahead!
Today's markets are brought to you by Bin & Barrel Storage Solutions. If it fits in a bin, it fits in a bin.
DNN is sponsored by the Mechanics' Guild. Levers, gears, pressure plates. We never ask what you're connecting them to.
This segment is brought to you by Whisker Wranglers, the fort's premier cat management service. Results not guaranteed. Or achieved.
Beard looking dull? Try Mason's Choice Beard Oil, made from the finest rendered tallow. Smell like a dwarf of means.
DNN is brought to you by Rocknut Roasts. Rocknut: it's a roast. You eat it. What more do you want?
Feeling a strange mood coming on? Visit Fey Supply Co. We stock every material a possessed craftsdwarf could ask for. Except that one.
DNN is sponsored by the Dining Hall Committee. Eat in the dining hall. Not on the stairs. We are begging you.
Tired of cave-ins? Trust Pillar Pals Support Engineering. We put the 'up' in 'holding the ceiling up.'
DNN is brought to you by the Fort Tavern. Live music, loud arguments, a mug for every dwarf. Fights at your own risk.
Bloodbrew Dwarven Rum: distilled from sugarcane, finished with regret. Bloodbrew. Ask your tavern keeper by name.
This hour is sponsored by Safe-T-Hatch. Keep the carp out, keep the goblins out, keep the in-laws out.
DNN Weather is brought to you by Roofs. Roofs: you can have one too. Talk to a mason today.
Lost a sock? Lost a boot? Lost the will to haul? Try the Stockpile Office lost-and-found, open whenever someone's there.
DNN is brought to you by Gutterflow Drainage. When the reservoir overflows, and it will, you'll want us on speed-lever.
Ironjaw Crossbow Bolts: now with more bolt! Ironjaw. Because the goblins aren't going to shoot themselves.
DNN is brought to you by the Fort Chandler. Tallow soap, wax, and absolutely nothing scented. Smell like the mountain intended.
Is your bedroom a two-by-one hole? Upgrade with Hollowstone Interiors. We smooth the walls, you feel like a noble.
This segment is sponsored by Grim & Sons Mortuary. We engrave your name right. Or at least the parts we can spell.
DNN is brought to you by Carp-Away Riverside Fencing. Swim safe. Or better yet, never swim at all.
Magma Plumbing: we pipe the magma where you want it and mostly not where you don't. Licensed, bonded, and singed.
Need a new mug? The Potters' Collective has thousands. Literally thousands. Please take some. Please.
DNN is brought to you by the Plump Helmet Growers' Association. Plump helmets: they're food, they're drink, they're a lifestyle.
Tantrum cover from Steadyhand Mutual. When a dwarf throws your chair across the tavern, we'll help you get another chair.
This hour of DNN is sponsored by the Hospital Gift Shop. Get-well socks, get-well splints, get-well soap.
DNN is brought to you by Deepmine Picks. Strike the earth, and keep striking it, until something shiny falls out.
Sore from hauling? Try the Mineral Soak at the bath channel. It's cold water from the brook, but we call it a spa.
The Ale Index is sponsored by Twice-Brewed Dwarven Wine. Twice-Brewed: brewed once, then brewed again, for reasons.
DNN is brought to you by Militia Mail. Every suit pre-dented for comfort. Join the squad, wear the steel, look the part.
Hate elves? So do we. Treefree Furniture: every piece carved from stone, so no elf ever weeps over your table.
DNN is sponsored by the Bookkeeper's Office. We count your stuff so you don't have to. Accuracy coming soon.
This hour is brought to you by Lantern Moss Lighting. Glows faintly, smells strongly, and tastes, we're told, of regret.
Pet trouble? Call Pasture Pals Animal Training. We'll teach your war dog to sit, stay, and only bite goblins.
DNN is brought to you by the Carved Throne Gallery. Chairs fit for a baron, priced for a hauler, sized for neither.
Find peace at the Fort Temple. Pray, meditate, or just sit quietly away from your coworkers. Open always.
DNN is brought to you by Rockseal Barrels. Rockseal: they don't leak, unless you drop them, which you will.
Thinking of moving to a bigger fort? Don't. Stay here. A message from the Expedition Leader's Office.
This segment is sponsored by Last Breath Coffins, now in stone, wood and premium glass. See yourself out in style.
DNN is brought to you by Bonecraft Novelties. Bone earrings, bone crowns, bone mugs. Don't ask whose bones.
Got vermin? Got a cat? Got another cat? Got eleven cats? Then you've already got Whisker Wranglers. Call us. Please.
DNN is brought to you by Quarry Fresh Stone. Every boulder hand-picked from the actual mountain. Taste the rock.
Overwhelmed by mandates? The Noble Compliance Office will make whatever the baron asked for, eventually, out of something.
This hour of DNN is brought to you by the Tavern Bards' Union. Songs, poems, dances. Nobody asked, and yet here we are.
Deepsweet Syrup Spread: sweet, sticky, and impossible to get out of a beard. Deepsweet. Commit to the beard.
DNN is brought to you by Pressure Plate Security. Uninvited guest? Stepped on the wrong tile? That's a Pressure Plate moment.
The Mechanics' Guild reminds you: never pull an unlabelled lever. Unless it looks fun. Paid for by the Mechanics' Guild.
DNN is sponsored by Deep Cellar Cheeses. Aged in the dark, served in the dark, smelled three levels up.
This broadcast is made possible by viewers like you, and by the Ale Index Trust, a wholly owned subsidiary of the tavern.

Ale Index at {drinks}. Tavern reacts with cautious cheering
Cat count reaches {cats}; vermin issue formal complaint
Stone stockpile at {stone}; masons say 'we could use more' out of habit

Forgotten beast still forgotten, sources say. Please keep it that way

Mayor holds meeting; meeting is about future meetings

Military drill postponed; the military is at the tavern

Horse stuck in the stairwell again; mechanics propose a 'horse lift'

Rumour: a dwarf drank water. DNN cannot independently confirm
Year {year} rated best year so far, by everyone living in it

Fort guard denies sleeping; snoring noted on the duty roster
Elf caravan sells wooden toys; dwarves react with polite horror
Mug shortage averted after potter discovers she made too many
Masons: 'all walls are good walls'; demolition crew disagrees
Trapper catches a rat; rat now the fort's unofficial mascot
Silk weaver works overtime; cave spiders remain unpaid

Sculptor's statue of a cat turns out to be an actual cat
Smith forges an anvil to forge anvils; philosophers in distress

Kobold spotted near stockpile; kobold denies everything, holding a sock
Dwarf wins argument with a door; door remains closed
Trainer tames a giant cave spider; nobody else will enter the room
Fort declares festival; festival identical to a normal day with more ale
Water wheel turns; mechanics call it 'basically perpetual'; it is not
Dwarf lost in the depths for three days found, asks for a mug
Chief medical dwarf announces cure: rest, splints, and 'not doing that'
Strange mood strikes a workshop; everyone else leaves quietly
Commander praises squad's dodging; squad had fled

Fishery says its catch outweighs the {meat} meat in stock, unprompted
Brewer reads ale label aloud, weeps
Beekeeper stung; beekeeper fine; bees 'disappointed'

Stairs confirmed to go both up and down; more after the break

Carp-fight engraving declared 'too intense' by young viewers

Unknown dwarf seen in noble's hat; mayor 'not amused, slightly amused'
{season} expected to continue for the rest of {season}, say experts
Dining hall table count reaches 'enough' for the first time in history
Child asks where ale comes from; brewer tells the truth; child shaken

Statue garden unveiled; visitors 'confused but supportive'
Test ballista shot hits the depot; depot fine, depot upset

sports.text: In the barracks, {citizen} sparred for six hours straight and lost every bout, but did so with tremendous enthusiasm.
Wrestling news: a recruit pinned a training dummy for a full count. The dummy will not be appealing the decision.
The Hauling League standings are in. The leaders carried 300 items this week, including one cat that did not want to be carried.
Dodging is up across the fort this {season}, mostly among dwarves avoiding the hospital's new bonesetter.
The great cheese-rolling is on! Competitors chased a wheel down the ramp. The wheel won. Three dwarves are in the hospital.
Sparring update: the militia commander and the captain of the guard fought to a draw, then had an ale about it.
{citizen2} set a new fort record in the hundred-urist dash, running from a carp. The carp has been disqualified.
Archery report: bolts fired today numbered in the hundreds. Bolts hitting the target: let's call it 'emerging talent.'
The Hauling League rookie of the season carried a boulder up four flights of stairs, then asked for another.
A big upset in the barracks: the smallest recruit in {fort} threw the biggest. There was biting, but officials say it counts.
The shield-blocking demonstration went well right up until the axe demonstration started next to it.
Swimming season is cancelled after the brook took a firm stance on the matter, backed by the carp.
Dodging champion {citizen} dodged every ball in today's tournament, and also dodged his chores. A true all-rounder.
The cheese-rolling final ended in controversy when the cheese was found to be a painted boulder. Investigation pending.
In mining sports, the annual Dig-Off saw two miners carve a tunnel in record time. Nobody knows where it leads.
Tavern darts is suspended after a dwarf used a throwing axe. Officials say it is 'technically a dart' but please don't.
Stair-racing returns to the main shaft. Rules: run up, run down, do not touch the haulers. The haulers are not part of this.
The Hauling League is investigating a dwarf who carried a bin full of socks and claimed it as 'one item.'
Barrel rolling: the champion rolled a full barrel the length of the dining hall without spilling a drop. Then drank it.
Sparring results: bruises, two black eyes, and one recruit who has finally learned which end of the spear is pointy.
The season's longest wrestling match lasted forty minutes before both dwarves fell asleep. Judges gave it to the floor.
Fans in the meeting hall chanted for the militia, then remembered they were the militia, and went to drill.
The cheese-rolling committee has introduced helmets this year. The cheese is unaffected and remains very fast.
Bout of the season: an off-duty marksdwarf versus a stubborn mule. The mule wins on points, and on kicks.
The hunting league reports a big week: one deer, two rabbits, and a squirrel that put up a genuinely impressive fight.
Our panel ranks the fort's best sparring partners. Number one is the wall, which has never lost.
Rock-tossing finals: {citizen} launched a boulder clear across the courtyard into the mason's window. Gold medal and a bill.
In axe-throwing, today's champion hit the bullseye ten times. The target has been replaced. Twice.
Quarterly fitness report: hauling up, sparring steady, and napping, alarmingly, now officially classed as a sport.
The fort's first bin-carrying relay ended when the second runner forgot what was in the bin and stopped to check.
Hammerdwarves report a strong training week. The training dummies report nothing. They have no mouths.
Dodge of the day: a hauler who sidestepped a falling boulder, two cats and a noble's mandate in a single move.
The tavern arm-wrestling bracket is down to two finalists. One of them is a bear. The bear is the bookmakers' favourite.
The barracks have banned the beard grab. Several veteran wrestlers are calling it the end of an era.
The great cheese-rolling drew {pop} spectators, which is everyone. No work was done. The cheese did great.
Sparring trends: the spear is out, the axe is in, and the crossbow remains 'for dwarves who don't like hugs.'
The Hauling League has added a new event, the Two-Barrel Waddle. Early reports say it is 'mostly falling.'
In marathon news, a dwarf walked from the depot to the deepest mine for one plump helmet. Locals call that 'commuting.'
A recruit blocked twelve blows in a row with her shield today. She is now asleep on the shield. Sports desk salutes her.
Barracks challenge: a veteran swordsdwarf versus a cat. The cat simply left. Judges awarded nothing to anyone.
{anchor2} reports the militia's dodging drills are going so well that nobody has seen the militia in days.

trade.text: The depot is open and {caravan_civ} traders have arrived with goods, opinions, and a very tired pack yak.
Elven merchants are offering wooden furniture again. Our broker says no, firmly, and from a safe distance.
Haggling tip from the trade desk: if the merchant laughs, you've offered too little. If they cry, you've won.
Caravan watch: no traders on the horizon yet. The depot clerk is staring at the road anyway, just in case.
The broker reports trading forty stone mugs for one bag of salt. The broker calls this 'a rout.'
Human traders at the depot are selling cloth and asking where the surface is. They were told: up. Just up.
Trade desk breaking: the {caravan_civ} caravan wants crafts. We have crafts. We have so many crafts. Haul the crafts.
Elves have refused a gift of a fine wooden bin. Our broker is 'stunned' and also 'fully aware of what he did.'
Export update: the fort's top export remains rock crafts, followed closely by more rock crafts.
Import news: the caravan brought cheese, cloth, and a dog. The dog was not for sale. The dog came in anyway.
Depot analysts say the outpost liaison is 'friendly, chatty, and asking an awful lot about our gem stockpile.'
The broker opened talks with a polite bow, a firm handshake and a decorated stone goblet. The standard opener.
Elves are offering goods made with no wood whatsoever. They're very proud. It's all cloth. Sad, sad cloth.
Trade tip: never trade away the last barrel. The tavern keeper asked us to say that. Twice. Holding a mallet.
{caravan_civ} merchants are unloading at the depot, and haulers are complaining at the depot. Commerce works.
The broker is haggling over a single steel bar. Day three. Both parties are now napping between offers.
Market watch: demand for crafted goods is high. Demand for elf-made toys remains at zero, as it has for centuries.
Merchants say our roasts are 'surprisingly good for underground cooking.' The cook would like to know what that means.
Record trade at the depot: three masterwork crowns for enough leather to clothe the whole militia. Good business.
Goblins have not arrived to trade. Goblins never arrive to trade. The trade desk reminds you to keep the gate shut.
Talks stalled after the merchant asked to see the bookkeeper's records. The bookkeeper's records are a rock.
{caravan_civ} traders asked for a 'more welcoming entrance.' We have a drawbridge and several traps. That is the welcome.
Broker {citizen} has closed a deal on twelve barrels of foreign wine. The tavern is preparing a respectful silence.
A word on prices: our gems are worth a lot, our mugs a little, and our broker is worth his weight in salt.
An elven envoy asked whether we cut down trees. We said no. The trade desk is not here to editorialise.
Depot traffic halted briefly when a pack horse refused to come inside. The horse has 'concerns about the ceiling.'
The liaison wants a list of goods we'd like next year. The list says 'ale' four times and 'more ale' once.
The caravan guards are lingering at the tavern. They're not shopping. They're just enjoying themselves.
Economists note the fort trades rocks for food at excellent rates, which means we are, technically, eating rocks.
Haggling tips, continued: insist the item is cursed. Elves fall for it every time. Humans sometimes buy two.
The caravan has left and the depot is quiet. The broker is counting the profits; the haulers are counting their bruises.

works.text: On the works desk: construction on {project} continues. Masons report 'steady progress' and 'a lot of dust in our beards.'
{project} is ahead of schedule. Sources say that's because nobody ever wrote down a schedule.
Engineers on {project} have found a cave. They have asked us not to say what is in the cave.
The architect says {project} will be 'the pride of {fort}.' At the moment it is a hole. A proud hole.
Work on {project} paused briefly while the miners argued about whether up was the correct direction.
